source.quote: Currently, our project backlog stands at $3.8 billion, which is slightly lower than last quarter.
Net debt to adjusted EBITDA was 1.1x at the end of the year which is at the lower end of our internal range of 1x to 2x.
We delivered a solid second quarter with net revenues in line with the outlook we provided during our Q1 call.
For 2021, we anticipate the lower to mid-single-digit organic net revenue growth.

We anticipate gross margin to be somewhere in the range of 52% to 53.5%, which reflects our expectation that the pandemic will continue to impact productivity, both within our operations and that of our clients and an anticipated meaningful increase in the cost of employee group benefits.

You've talked about -- or you've reiterated your expectation for low to mid-single-digit organic growth in 2021, which is consistent with what you had talked about last quarter.

source.quote: Our projected low to mid single-digit organic revenue growth for the year is underpinned with our expectation that Q1's organic retraction should turn the corner in Q2.
Q1 earnings were slightly ahead of our expectations, with adjusted net income from continuing operations increasing 3% to $56 million, which represented 6.4% of net revenue.
We continue to expect 2021 full-year organic net revenue growth to be in the low to mid-single digits or 1% to 5%, but with a slight shift in mix relative to our previous thoughts.
Adjusted EBITDA margin is now projected to be 15% to 16% of net revenue.
And as for adjusted diluted EPS, we now expect to achieve 4% to 7% growth in 2021 compared to 2020, where our previous guidance was for low to mid-single-digit growth or 1% to 5%.

Our increased EPS guidance for 4% to 7% growth in 2021 is predicated on our solid performance in the first half of the year, the strength of our backlog and our more than $1 billion in award notifications that aren't yet booked into backlog.

I would say all things being equal, that we do expect we'll be able to maintain a lower tax rate relative to the 27% to 28% we started this year with.
On a constant currency basis, we grew net revenue by over 2%, which was in line, actually a little better than our expectation we had coming into the quarter.
Overall, the Q2 performance of our U.S. business was in line with our expectations, with 7.4% organic revenue retraction in contrast to organic growth last year.
And we expect Cardno to increase our annual net revenues by more than $350 million in 2022.
